source_contracts: GEM lock exists before display resources initialize
All migrated GEM paths share the same private mutex
Last close retains device around core release
DRM file operations retain unsigned offset requirement
Device and callback ownership keeps successful display module resident
Client list and locks precede cdev exposure
Feature singleton publishes after complete cdev and device setup
Feature lookup cannot reenter initialization
Client event state exists before notification publication
Old cdev identities cannot open the current singleton
Raw events cannot overflow the 4 KiB event budget
DSI receive alignment rejects unsigned overflow
Debug notification and work drain before buffers free
Panel withdraws the draining pwrkey callback before teardown
CPU read/write waits use the Linux reservation usage enum
Base and private GEM objects share reservation state
Failed GEM setup can remove an initialized inactive-list entry
VRAM pages release before their VMA node is freed
Embedded DRM client owns its unregister callback
Log formatter reports only bytes present in its local buffer
Log reads serialize with ring writes
Procfs stack writes reserve space for the terminator
limits: Extracted functions with simulated allocator, workers, DRM reference counting, notifier and OF services. Tests do not establish kernel scheduling, DRM atomic commits, hardware fences, display firmware, suspend/resume or phone compatibility.
